newsitem.title: GREECE: Greek teachers in sixth week of strike.
newsitem.headline: Greek teachers in sixth week of strike.

text.p: Greek state high school teachers began their sixth week on strike on Tuesday, raising prospects that the school year might be extended to make up for lost teaching hours.
"We must find a solution. Thousands of teaching hours have been lost. One option is to hold lessons on Saturdays and cut holidays," an Education Ministry official told Reuters.

The teachers are striking to press for higher salaries, but Education Minister Gerassimos Arsenis has said they are among the best paid public servants and this year's state budget cannot afford more funds for any particular working group.
Officials said some 60 percent of the country's high schools have been closed during the strike. Parents' organisations have urged an immediate compromise to end the strike.
Civil servants were also holding a nationwide 24-hour strike on Tuesday for better wages and pensions but government officials said participation in the stoppage was limited.
